claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr baseline is primarily a single-phase BCC matrix with no or minimal nanoscale precipitates.
The aging-induced precipitates in HfNbTaTiZr are nanoscale.
The proposed precipitates are enriched in both Ta and Zr.
The precipitates form through limited solid-state segregation during aging.
The precipitates have thermal expansion properties distinct from those of the BCC matrix.
Thermal expansion mismatch between precipitates and the BCC matrix generates local internal stress fields.
Precipitate-induced internal stresses impede dislocation glide during creep at 1250 °C.
Precipitate-induced internal stresses increase resistance to deformation during cold rolling.
Precipitate-induced internal stresses modify lattice dynamics and consequently alter elastic moduli.
A common precipitate-induced internal-stress mechanism explains creep behavior, cold-rolling hardening, and temperature-dependent elastic moduli in HfNbTaTiZr.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, aged HfNbTaTiZr will have increased yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, aged HfNbTaTiZr will have a reduced creep rate at 1250 °C.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, aged HfNbTaTiZr will have enhanced or otherwise modified elastic moduli, especially at intermediate temperatures.
Changes in mechanical and elastic responses will correlate with precipitate volume fraction and spatial distribution.
Aging at 600, 700, and 800 °C for 30 and 60 minutes provides a controlled intervention for comparison with the as-cast alloy.
The proposed response boundaries are creep at 1250 °C and elastic-modulus measurements from 293 to 1100 K.
The direct relationship between precipitates, internal stresses, and the three response classes in HfNbTaTiZr remains unconfirmed.
